mmc5racing.short_description: A retro top-down racer in the eight-bit tradition: five laps, a running clock and no frills.
mmc5racing.description:
MMC5Racing is a compact retro racer presented in the classic overhead style: pixel cars, a winding track and a lap counter that runs to five. Its title nods to the NES's famous MMC5 mapper chip, and the page's screenshot shows the game running on a CRT, leaning fully into the old-school console aesthetic.

The itch page itself carries no written description, so details are deliberately thin — what you get is a small, free browser racer whose HUD tracks your current lap time and your total while you chase down lap five. If that sounds like your kind of time attack, it costs nothing to try, and the original itch.io page is the place to follow the developer, Nao_u838861.
mmc5racing.how_to_play: Complete five laps of the track as fast as you can. The HUD splits your time into a per-lap clock and a running total, so the goal is a fast total over five clean laps. For anything beyond what the page shows, the original itch.io page is the authoritative source.
mmc5racing.controls: See the original itch.io page for the developer's control notes.
mmc5racing.tips:
The lap clock exists to show you where you are losing pace — compare it against your total after each lap.
Five laps go by quickly, so a clean first lap sets the tone for the whole run.
mmc5racing.features:
Top-down retro racing in a bright eight-bit style
Lap-based runs with the counter set to five laps
Per-lap and total time readouts on the HUD
Plays directly in the browser as an HTML5 game
Released in October 2026 by Nao_u838861
mmc5racing.editorial_take: We picked this one up precisely because it is such a small, unexplained thing: a five-lap retro racer that shows up with a CRT screenshot and zero marketing copy. It is a two-minute time-attack snack for fans of overhead NES-era racing rather than a deep simulation, and that is exactly the charm. If you enjoy discovering half-documented oddities on itch.io, add it to the pile.
mmc5racing.meta_description: Race five laps in MMC5Racing, a free retro top-down racer that runs in your browser. No download, no account — just an eight-bit time attack.

rainbow-city.short_description: Knock color off a colossal crystal and ship it home to grow a rainbow city.
rainbow-city.description:
A giant crystal core sits at the edge of town, and every hit you land knocks loose a little more color. Rainbow City turns that one idea into a whole economy: send the color home and the city grows — fill the Commons, add homes, open the mines, and watch an ordinary street gradually turn into a rainbow.

The clever part is that the color is physical. Every chip you knock off falls, piles up and rolls, so part of the game is literally shoveling paint. Build routes and carriers haul the loose color in while hammer choirs keep chipping at the core while you are away. Later on there is research, ore and a reset loop with permanent upgrades, plus an AUTO mode (beta) with x1, x2 and x4 pacing if you would rather just watch the machine you built do its thing.

It plays on phone and PC, saves in your browser, and was released by gelwater in October 2026.
rainbow-city.how_to_play: Tap or hold the core to break color off it, then tap or hold the loose color to send it home. Tap buildings to upgrade them, build routes so carriers can haul color in for you, and let the hammer choirs chip away while you are gone. Drag to pan the view and use the wheel or a pinch to zoom; progress saves in your browser.
rainbow-city.controls:
Tap or hold – break the core / send loose color home
Tap buildings – upgrade them
Drag – pan the view
Mouse wheel or pinch – zoom
rainbow-city.tips:
Build routes early — carriers are how the city grows while you are busy at the core.
Permanent upgrades survive the reset loop, so an early reset that unlocks research pays off later.
AUTO mode (beta) is honest about what it is: if you want an idle screensaver, set the pace and let it build.
rainbow-city.features:
Physics-driven color: every chip falls, piles up and rolls
Carriers, smashers, mine carts, flow crews and gliders, each with their own job
Research, ore and a reset loop with permanent upgrades
AUTO mode (beta) with x1, x2 and x4 pacing
Plays on phone and PC with drag-to-pan and wheel/pinch zoom
Saves in your browser, no account needed
Released October 2026 by gelwater
rainbow-city.editorial_take: Rainbow City is our favorite kind of idle game: one absurd, tactile verb that slowly expands into routes, crews, mines and prestige. The physics angle gives it a texture most clickers lack, since the color genuinely piles and rolls instead of just ticking up in a counter. If you like watching a little machine hum, or you want a city builder you can run from a phone in portrait, this is an easy recommendation.
rainbow-city.meta_title: Play Rainbow City Online - Idle Physics City Builder
rainbow-city.meta_description: Chip color off a giant crystal core, route it home and grow a rainbow city in your browser. A free idle city builder with real physics and an AUTO mode.

the-cat-did-it.short_description: You are the cat, the house is spotless, and the afternoon is young.
the-cat-did-it.description:
One tidy house. One quiet afternoon. One cat — and you are the cat. In The Cat Did It, AmyGood's 3D destruction sandbox, everything in the living room exists to be knocked off a table: mugs, vases, plates, candles, the fruit bowl. Almost all of it breaks.

It does not stop at pawing things off shelves. Pull the tablecloth out from under the place settings, topple the bookshelf, tip the plant into the robot vacuum's path and let the vacuum finish the job, or drag a full roll of toilet paper through three rooms. Meanwhile she is somewhere in the house — if she catches you mid-mischief she scoops you up and sets you back on the sofa, though being cute at the right moment might make her forget why she walked over.

The afternoon ends with the bill: a note on the fridge itemizing every broken thing, every paw print and every metre of toilet paper, plus a before-and-after card that rates the damage somewhere between mild inconvenience and natural disaster. Pick Prince the tuxedo, shy Marmalade, or build a cat that looks like yours — and note that the house itself changes every afternoon. It is an early version that the developer says will keep growing, playable free in the browser on phone or computer.
the-cat-did-it.how_to_play: Roam the house and knock over, pull down or drag whatever looks satisfying, then end the afternoon with a nap to read the damage bill. Watch out for her: getting caught means being carried back to the sofa, so timing and escape routes matter. The fridge note and before-and-after card score exactly how much worse you made everything.
the-cat-did-it.controls:
Move – WASD / arrow keys, or the on-screen joystick on phone
Jump – Space, or the Jump button
Paw – E, or the Paw button
Look around – drag
Nap and end the afternoon – N, or the Nap button
the-cat-did-it.tips:
Work room by room so you always have an exit before she turns the corner.
Being cute is a legitimate tactic — if she comes over and finds you being adorable, she may forget the vase.
The bill counts everything, so the big furniture is where the numbers are.
the-cat-did-it.features:
3D cat-chaos sandbox built with Three.js, playable in the browser
Everything on the shelves can fall and almost all of it breaks
Chain disasters: tablecloths, bookshelves, robot vacuums and toilet paper
An owner who patrols the house and scoops you back to the sofa if she catches you
End-of-day damage bill with a before-and-after rating card
Three cats to play, including a custom one that looks like yours
The house changes every afternoon
Free, no download and no account, on phone or computer
the-cat-did-it.editorial_take: The premise writes itself, and the game actually delivers it — the itemized fridge bill at the end of the afternoon is the joke that keeps paying. It is early days: the developer openly calls it a growing first version and is collecting players' real cats' worst habits for future missions. Even so, as a cozy-chaos sandbox it already stands out, and we recommend it to anyone who has ever owned a cat and a bookshelf.
the-cat-did-it.meta_title: Play The Cat Did It Online - Cat Chaos Sandbox
the-cat-did-it.meta_description: Be the cat in The Cat Did It: knock over a spotless house, dodge the owner and get billed for every break. A free 3D chaos sandbox in your browser.

pong.short_description: A classic Pong clone built on camera as the first project of a Spanish learn-to-code series.
pong.description:
This is Pong, but with a backstory: it is the first project of PROGRAMAR MAL, a Spanish-language YouTube series in which the developer learns programming through small projects and shows the entire process along the way. The clone itself is the classic you expect — two paddles, a ball, and points scored when the other side misses.

It is a simple, honest browser build made in Unity, presented in Spanish like the series around it. There is a Player vs Player mode for local two-player matches on one keyboard, with the second player on the arrow keys, so it doubles as a quick coffee-break duel. If you read Spanish and are curious how it was made, the series walks through the whole development process step by step.
pong.how_to_play: Move your paddle to return the ball and score when your opponent misses. The Player vs Player mode puts two players on one keyboard for a local match.
pong.controls:
Player 1 – W to move the paddle up, S to move it down
Player 2 (Player vs Player mode only) – Up arrow to move up, Down arrow to move down
pong.tips:
Watch the ball, not your paddle — in Pong the return angle is decided at contact.
In PvP, mirror your opponent's movement to keep the center covered.
pong.features:
Classic Pong clone playable in the browser
Local two-player Player vs Player mode on one keyboard
Built in Unity as the first project of the PROGRAMAR MAL series
Spanish-language presentation, matching the series
Part of a YouTube series that documents the whole learning process
pong.editorial_take: We are featuring it for the meta-game: this is a working Pong made by someone learning to program in public, which is exactly the kind of honest artifact itch.io is good at. As a game it is precisely what a Pong clone should be — instant to parse, quick to duel — and the local PvP mode makes it a decent two-minute office match. Watch the series if you want to see it get built.
pong.meta_title: Play Programar Mal Pong Online - Browser Pong Clone
pong.meta_description: Play a classic Pong clone in your browser, with local two-player PvP on one keyboard. Built in Unity for the Spanish learn-to-code series PROGRAMAR MAL.

golem-quest.short_description: Assemble minerals, raise your golem and send it questing in Barribob's short RPG prototype.
golem-quest.description:
Golem Quest is a short RPG prototype from Barribob — the developer behind Magic Archery — built as a side experiment between other projects. The pitch is in the title: create an unstoppable golem.

The page's text is brief, but the screenshots show the shape of it: a pixel-art world where you pick quests in areas like Welcome Hills and Mystic Grove, manage a loadout of available and unlocked minerals, and grow your golem across stats like Physique, Finesse, Mind and Influence as it levels. The developer notes that if a sequel to Magic Archery ever happens, it might look something like this — so treat it as an early sketch of an idea rather than a finished game, and have fun with it.
golem-quest.how_to_play: Pick a quest area, equip your golem with the minerals you have unlocked, and send it out — the four stat lines (Physique, Finesse, Mind, Influence) and the golem's level are your build. The prototype explains little in text, so experimenting with mineral loadouts between quests is the intended loop.
golem-quest.controls: See the original itch.io page for the developer's control notes.
golem-quest.tips:
Change Quest sits on the HUD, so hopping between areas to test different mineral builds is cheap.
Keep an eye on which minerals are still locked — expanding the loadout is how the golem grows.
golem-quest.features:
Short RPG prototype built in Godot, playable in the browser
Create and upgrade a golem from a loadout of minerals
Four visible stats: Physique, Finesse, Mind and Influence
Quest areas such as Welcome Hills and Mystic Grove
Pixel-art side view
From Barribob, the developer of Magic Archery
golem-quest.editorial_take: This is a prototype in the honest sense — a few screens, a mineral loadout and a lot of unspoken systems — but that is exactly why it is interesting: you get to peek at an early idea from the Magic Archery developer before it becomes anything. Low commitment, free, and worth twenty minutes if you like watching game designs take their first steps.
golem-quest.meta_title: Play Golem Quest Online - Free Browser RPG Prototype
golem-quest.meta_description: Build a mineral-powered golem and send it questing in Golem Quest, a free short RPG prototype you can play right in your browser.

taiwanese-oyster-omelette.short_description: A night-market cooking sim from Taiwan: spread the batter, mind the flame, flip at gold.
taiwanese-oyster-omelette.description:
Oyster omelette — 蚵仔煎 — is a Taiwanese night-market classic, and this Traditional-Chinese cooking sim turns one order of it into a small, tidy ritual. The page lets the food do the talking: across seven steps you spread the starch batter to wrap the oysters, manage the burner flame, flip the omelette once the edges turn golden, and plate it up.

Every pan gets graded. The result card scores your omelette and breaks the verdict into seven meters — crispiness, batter chewiness, the egg, the greens, the sauce, the flip and more — crowned with a title like The Unyielding Oyster Omelette for the ones that survived seven flips and still did not fall. Ending cards are collected in a gallery, and the game closes with an invitation to come back to the pan. The screenshots show a tall, portrait-friendly layout, so it reads like it was designed with phones in mind.
taiwanese-oyster-omelette.how_to_play: Follow the seven steps as prompted: drag the batter to enclose the oysters, adjust the flame with the heat controls, flip when the edges turn golden, and take it off the pan when both sides are done. Your score depends on doing each step cleanly, and every run earns a graded result card for the gallery.
taiwanese-oyster-omelette.controls:
On-screen touch controls — the step prompts and UI are in Traditional Chinese
See the original itch.io page for the developer's notes
taiwanese-oyster-omelette.tips:
Watch the edges, not the clock — the game itself tells you to flip when the rim turns golden.
Heat is a dial, not a switch: the flame controls sit by the pan, and your final grade reflects how you used them.
taiwanese-oyster-omelette.features:
Traditional-Chinese cooking sim about Taiwan's night-market oyster omelette
Seven-step fry: batter, oysters, flame control, flip and plating
Final grade with seven quality meters and a result title
Ending card gallery to collect across runs
Portrait-friendly layout that suits phones
HTML5 browser game, released October 2026
taiwanese-oyster-omelette.editorial_take: Hyper-specific food sims are a quiet strength of itch.io, and this is a lovely specimen: no plot, no meta, just one dish and the seven small skills between you and a perfect pan of 蚵仔煎. The language barrier is minimal because the steps are visual, and the graded result card gives it just enough score-chasing spine. Come hungry.
taiwanese-oyster-omelette.meta_title: Play Taiwanese Oyster-Omelette Online - Cooking Sim
taiwanese-oyster-omelette.meta_description: Cook a Taiwanese night-market oyster omelette in seven steps: batter, flame, flip and get graded. A free Traditional-Chinese cooking sim in your browser.

carbineball.short_description: Pinball with a twist: your cursor is a character that bumps the ball and packs two revolvers.
carbineball.description:
Carbineball is anttihaavikko's take on pinball, built solo from scratch in a weekend for Ludum Dare 60. The board will look familiar, but the way you touch the ball is not: your mouse cursor is basically a character on the table that can bump the ball directly, and it is equipped with two revolvers so you can also interact with it from range — the designer compares the result to Pong, Breakout and Arkanoid as much as to pinball.

Scoring runs on an arcade multiplier. Bumping the ball builds your multiplier, but it only keeps climbing if you shoot between bumps, and there is a sun bumper pad at the bottom of the screen that raises the multiplier while putting you one bad save away from losing the ball off the edge — which is, of course, game over. The board is split into three distinct sections with their own aims, and a rotating bonus game is picked every 30 seconds, paying out far more than normal play and nudging you to keep rotating.

There are also several characters and balls to unlock, each with unique bonuses, strengths and weaknesses, plus online leaderboards for the scorechasers.
carbineball.how_to_play: Move your cursor into the ball to bump it, and weave shots from your revolvers between bumps to keep the multiplier climbing. Chase the rotating bonus game every 30 seconds, treat the sun bumper as a calculated risk, and do not let the ball leave the board.
carbineball.controls:
Move – mouse cursor (bump the ball by moving into it)
Shoot – your mouse buttons fire the two revolvers
See the original itch.io page for the developer's notes
carbineball.tips:
The multiplier only grows if you alternate: bump, then shoot, then bump again.
The sun bumper pad is the fastest multiplier on the table and the fastest way to lose the ball — approach it on purpose, not by accident.
Rotate objectives with the 30-second bonus game; camping one section leaves the biggest payouts untouched.
carbineball.features:
Pinball-breakout hybrid where your cursor is a character on the board
Two revolvers for ranged play against the ball
Arcade multiplier that only builds when you shoot between bumps
Risk/reward sun bumper pad above the drain
Three board sections plus a rotating bonus game every 30 seconds
Unlockable characters and balls with unique bonuses and weaknesses
Online leaderboards
Made solo from scratch in a weekend for Ludum Dare 60, in Godot
carbineball.editorial_take: Plenty of jam games riff on pinball; very few make your hand a participant. Carbineball's cursor-as-character idea turns every save into a body check and every gap in your shooting into a lost multiplier, which gives the whole loop a much more physical feel than the genre usually has. It is a Ludum Dare build that plays tight rather than thin — recommended for leaderboard climbers and anyone bored of plain flippers.
carbineball.meta_title: Play Carbineball Online - Pinball With Revolvers
carbineball.meta_description: Bump, shoot and multiplier your way up the leaderboards in Carbineball, a free browser pinball hybrid where your cursor carries two revolvers.

living-scraps.short_description: You scrap robots for a living. Talk to them first — then decide who survives.
living-scraps.description:
Living Scraps is a short adventure about a robot whose job is scrapping other robots. The quota is stated plainly in the game itself: scrap at least three of them, and the more you scrap, the better your rating. It is up to you who survives and who gets scrapped — the developer calls the whole thing a psychological drama, and the label fits.

Before any scrap process starts, there is a conversation. You can scan a robot, ask what its condition is, ask what its function is, or make polite chat — the small talk is where these machines get their personalities, and the dialogue options are where the game does its quiet work. Whether you rush the quota or talk to every unit first is entirely your call, and the game is short enough to try both.
living-scraps.how_to_play: Meet each robot, talk with it — scan it, ask about its condition or function, or just chat — and then either start the scrap process or let it walk away. Your workplace rating rewards scrapping at least three robots, and how you reach that number is the story you are telling.
living-scraps.controls:
Point-and-click dialogue choices (a cursor selects from the option list)
See the original itch.io page for the developer's control notes
living-scraps.tips:
Talking first is optional, and it is where the whole game lives — the scrap button will still be there after the chat.
The quota needs three; nothing says the three have to be the first three you meet.
living-scraps.features:
Short narrative adventure about deciding which robots get scrapped
Dialogue-first structure: scan, question, make polite chat
A quota and rating system that pressures your conscience
Psychological drama framing, as the developer calls it
Playable in the browser, also distributed for Windows
living-scraps.editorial_take: A tiny game with a very old question in new plating: the quota wants three, the robots want to keep talking, and the gap between those two facts is the entire experience. It belongs to the same family of conscience-versus-paperwork games as Papers, Please, at a fraction of the scale — a coffee-break moral puzzle you can replay both ways. Short, sharp, recommended.
living-scraps.meta_title: Play Living Scraps Online - Robot Drama Adventure
living-scraps.meta_description: Interrogate robots before you scrap them in Living Scraps, a free short browser adventure about quotas, conscience and polite chat with machines.

abattlacus.short_description: A roguelike autobattler fought on an abacus, where every row you win is added to your purse.
abattlacus.description:
Abattlacus is a roguelike autobattler played, literally, on an abacus — made in 72 hours by FunB4nan for Ludum Dare 60. You build a team of beads, position fighters and archers, and combine their abilities with powerful artifacts, then let the rows resolve on their own.

The abacus is not just skin: every row becomes part of an equation. Victories add to your earnings, defeats subtract money and lives, and a Fairy can turn addition into multiplication. Between battles you spend your rewards on new beads and artifacts, stacking the combinations that will carry the next run — or watching one bad subtraction end it.
abattlacus.how_to_play: Build a team of beads and place your fighters and archers before the row resolves itself — this is an autobattler, so the fighting runs without input. Win rows to add to your earnings, spend the money between battles on new beads and artifacts, and keep an eye on the Fairy: it turns your additions into multiplications.
abattlacus.controls: See the original itch.io page for the developer's control notes.
abattlacus.tips:
Positioning is your main input once a row starts — put fighters where they absorb and archers where they shoot.
A lost row subtracts twice, hitting both your money and your lives, so a risky board costs more than it looks.
The Fairy is the strongest arithmetic on the board: multiplication beats stacking additions.
abattlacus.features:
Autobattler roguelike themed on an abacus, with rows as equations
Team building with beads, fighters and archers
Artifacts that combine with unit abilities
Victories add earnings, defeats subtract money and lives
A Fairy that turns addition into multiplication
Made in 72 hours for Ludum Dare 60, in Godot
abattlacus.editorial_take: Theme and mechanics rarely agree this precisely: on an abacus, winning really is addition, and the game makes you feel every subtraction. It is jam-scoped, so do not expect a long meta, but as a systems toy it is genuinely novel — recommended for autobattler fans who want their number-go-up to have beads on it.
abattlacus.meta_title: Play Abattlacus Online - Abacus Autobattler Roguelike
abattlacus.meta_description: Fight on an abacus in Abattlacus, a free browser autobattler roguelike where wins add money, defeats subtract lives and a Fairy multiplies it all.

legendum.short_description: Live many lives in an idle RPG where the world remembers what your last life did.
legendum.description:
Legendum is an incremental idle RPG about becoming a legend one lifetime at a time. You start as a nobody in a fantasy world and live a full life — young and sharp at first, slower of body as the years wear on while your skills remain — and when that life is done, another begins, in a world your previous deeds shaped. Spare a goblin in one life and you may meet that same goblin as a trader in the next.

The systems stack neatly on top of that idea. Combat is an idle horde fight where your build matters: an armored knight, a ranger striking from afar, or a powerful wizard, outfitted however you equip them. Between battles you manage a daily schedule — the page's example is a farmhand who studies a holy text at dawn, tends the fields by day and unwinds in the tavern at night. The world itself is your skill tree: your chronicle is a branching web of places, people and secrets, some paths visible from the start and others hidden until you explore. And underneath it all runs a story that spans generations, with each life pulling back another layer of a dark plot that one of them will finish.

This browser version is a demo of a full game planned for Steam, and it currently offers two origins — Farmhand and the work-in-progress Scholar. It is rated 4.6 out of 5 on itch.io, and the developer is actively collecting feedback through a form and a Discord server.
legendum.how_to_play: Choose an origin for your life — in the demo, Farmhand or Scholar — then split each day between training, work and rest while your idle horde battles resolve on their own. Explore the chronicle to open new paths, make choices that the next life will inherit, and see how far your legend climbs before old age catches up.
legendum.controls: See the original itch.io page for the developer's control notes.
legendum.tips:
Treat the daily schedule as your build: what a farmhand does at dawn compounds over a lifetime.
Some chronicle paths stay hidden until you explore, so push past the obvious branches.
Choices echo forward — the goblin you spare today can be the trader who sells to you next life.
legendum.features:
Incremental idle RPG where you live many successive lives in one world
Deeds persist: the world your next life inherits is shaped by the last one
Idle horde combat with knight, ranger and wizard builds
Full-lifetime aging: the body slows while skills remain
Daily schedule management between battles
The chronicle — a branching web of places, people and secrets — acts as the skill tree
A multi-generation story with a dark plot underneath
Free browser demo of a Steam-planned full version; Farmhand and Scholar (WIP) available
Rated 4.6 out of 5 on itch.io, built in Godot
legendum.editorial_take: Most idle games only ask how big your number should get; Legendum asks who you were when you got it. The generational memory — a spared goblin returning as a trader — is the standout hook, and with a 4.6 rating on itch it is one of the strongest debuts we have listed in this genre. The demo's two origins are enough to feel the loop; wishlist it if the full version's promise lands for you the way it did for us.
legendum.meta_title: Play Legendum - Free Idle RPG Browser Demo
legendum.meta_description: Live many lives in Legendum, a free browser idle RPG demo where your deeds shape the world your next life inherits. Fight, age and rise into legend.
